verdict_note: From reading only: no build, no test, no GUI. Line anchors are crates/hsk-studio-native-host at fc7f4215. The core fix holds. offscreen::run (offscreen.rs:45) and window::run (window.rs:284) are one-line wrappers over diag::observed (diag.rs:101). The inner bodies take only args and never touch the HostRun, so every return of run_scene and run_window yields exactly one finish (diag.rs:105). That covers the usage refusals, Vulkan refusals, document and gui refusals, event_loop and create_window failures, timeout, focus violation and success. A panic yields one send(PANIC_OUTCOME) (diag.rs:109) and then resume_unwind. HostRun::send refuses a second frame itself (diag.rs:82 terminal.is_some -> Closed), and observe's terminal_closed also refuses after a delivered terminal. studio-vk sends exactly one frame on every parse or caller refusal (studio-vk.rs:56-61) and none for help. A delivery error never changes the result of the library entries. The JSONL line is well formed: every string is a constant or hex, and the HSKO offsets 5, 6, 8..16 and 24..32 match the observe wire v1 header. Caller flags cannot inject into the line, and on every command line that parse accepts, run_flags tokenises exactly as parse does. All five findings are low. F1, F2 and F4 are small fixes in owned paths (bin/studio-vk.rs and the new test file). F3 is in diag.rs (owned). F5 is pre-existing and outside the owned run entries, so it should be named, not fixed here.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. std::env::args() is documented to panic during iteration on a non-Unicode argument. On Windows that means an argument with an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate, which is a legal NTFS file name.
findings.severity: low (a zero-frame path against the new contract 'every run but help sends one terminal observe frame, refusals included' (cli.rs USAGE, README, DESCRIPTOR); exit 101 is outside the documented exit table; it needs a non-Unicode argv)
findings.where: src/bin/studio-vk.rs:12 (std::env::args().skip(1).collect(), before any HostRun exists); :13 cli::parse and :20 cli::caller also run before HostRun::new (:28) and outside catch_unwind; parse reads --script files (cli.rs --script -> script::read, script.rs:104)
findings.what: Everything before HostRun::new runs with no sink and no catch_unwind. A non-Unicode argument panics in args() at :12, so the process exits 101 with no frame and no 'error usage/...' line. The frame guarantee for refusals also depends on cli::parse and its --script file read never panicking. I did not check script::read for panics.
findings.scenario: studio-vk offscreen --document <a path holding U+D800 as a lone surrogate> --observe o.jsonl: exit 101, o.jsonl is never created.
findings.fix: Read std::env::args_os() and refuse a non-UTF-8 argument as HostError::Usage (for example 'argument_encoding') through the same refusal arm (studio-vk.rs:56-61). Read the --observe value with to_str() where it is Unicode. Optionally construct the HostRun before cli::parse, so parse can also run under observed().
findings.test: #[cfg(windows)] in tests/fix_host_terminal_frame.rs: spawn studio-vk with OsString::from_wide(&[0xD800]) as a --document value plus a valid --observe; expect exit 2 and exactly one validation line.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. eprintln! is documented to panic when the stderr write fails. Rust's Windows stderr treats only an invalid handle as success, not a closed pipe.
findings.severity: low (a delivery failure changes studio-vk's exit code and suppresses a successful run's receipt; needs a closed stderr pipe; new in this lane, because the base wrote nothing to stderr on success)
findings.where: src/bin/studio-vk.rs:36-38 (if let Some(Err(e)) = host.terminal() { eprintln!("observe_undelivered ...") }), which runs before :40 println! of the receipt; src/diag.rs:172 (stderr sink write fails -> DeliveryError::Indeterminate)
findings.what: With no --observe, the frame goes to stderr. If stderr is a pipe whose reader is gone, LineSink returns Indeterminate. main then calls eprintln! on the same broken stderr, which panics. The process exits 101 instead of 0, and the receipt line at :40 is never printed. The doc line 'a delivery error never changes the run's result' (diag.rs HostRun doc) holds for the library entries but not for the binary's exit code.
findings.scenario: A supervisor reads studio-vk's stdout receipt and closes its stderr pipe early. studio-vk offscreen --size 8x8 then exits 101 with no receipt, where the base exited 0 and printed the receipt.
findings.fix: Write the undelivered note with let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr().lock(), ...), and print the receipt before the note. Apply the same to the unreachable HostRun::new arm at :31.
findings.test: Factor the tail of main into a fn taking (result, terminal, stdout: &mut dyn Write, stderr: &mut dyn Write) -> i32. Assert that a failing stderr writer with Ok(line) still returns 0 and writes the line.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. No current call site reuses a HostRun: the 18 test helpers, as_caller and studio-vk each build a fresh one (checked in the diff).
findings.severity: low (an API hazard: a silent zero-frame run, with terminal() reporting another run's receipt; no caller does this today)
findings.where: src/diag.rs:101-112 (observed runs the body unconditionally, then let _ = host.finish(..)), :81-84 (send returns Closed without touching self.terminal), :70 (terminal())
findings.what: The entries take &mut HostRun, so a caller can pass one HostRun to a second offscreen::run or window::run. The second run executes in full (device, window, capture, writes). Its frame is refused with Closed and discarded. host.terminal() still returns the first run's Ok(receipt), so a caller that checks terminal() after run 2 believes run 2's frame was delivered. The same applies to a panic in run 2. The lane design reads 'a second frame is refused', which is true, but nothing tells the caller.
findings.scenario: let mut host = HostRun::new(..); offscreen::run(&a, &mut host)?; offscreen::run(&b, &mut host)?; assert!(host.terminal().unwrap().is_ok()). Both pass, and run b sent no frame.
findings.fix: In observed, refuse before running the body when host.terminal().is_some() (a typed Usage refusal, for example 'host_run_finished', that opens nothing). Alternatively, make the entries take HostRun by value and return its terminal with the result. The first is the smaller change and keeps the approved signature.
findings.test: In tests/fix_host_terminal_frame.rs: a second offscreen::run(&clear_args(0, 48), &mut host) on a finished HostRun returns the typed refusal, the sink still holds one frame, and terminal() is unchanged.

Unlike the sibling crates' process tests, they do not set CREATE_NO_WINDOW. studio-vk is a console-subsystem binary (no windows_subsystem attribute). From a runner with no console, each of the 10 spawns opens a console window. findings.certainty: READ; not run. Pre-existing at c8fca900; this lane neither introduces nor changes it.
findings.severity: low (a resource leak across an unwind or an early event-loop error; it matters only to a library caller that catches the resumed panic or survives the Err, a path the lane now advertises; outside the owned paths (window.rs run entries only), so name it rather than fix it here)
findings.where: src/window.rs:154-190 (Watch: stop flag plus JoinHandle; finish() is the only stopper; no Drop impl), :317 Watch::spawn, :336 watch: Some(watch), :354 event_loop.run_app(&mut app).map_err(..)? (an Err returns before App::finish), App::finish (watch.take() then w.finish())
findings.what: Watch::finish is the only place that sets the stop flag of the hsk-foreground-watch thread. On an unwind out of run_window, or an early return from run_app Err, App drops with watch: Some. The JoinHandle detaches, and the thread keeps sampling the foreground window every 1 ms for the rest of the process. The unwind itself is sound: winit 0.30.13 windows event_loop.rs:422-425 calls reset_runner() before resume_unwind, so App is not still borrowed by the runner; observed then sends one frame and resumes. No std Mutex is held across the run: document.rs intern and the vulkan owner's statics recover from poisoning.
findings.scenario: A host that wraps window::run in its own catch_unwind (or gets HostError::Window("event_loop") from run_app) keeps a 1 ms polling thread alive after the run.
findings.fix: impl Drop for Watch that stores stop = true (joining is optional). Owned by a native-host window lane, not this one, unless the lead extends the owned paths.
findings.test: A unit test in window.rs: spawn a Watch, drop it, and assert the thread's stop flag is set and join completes (for example via an Arc strong-count or a returned handle).

answers.one_frame_every_exit_path: Yes for the library entries: every return of run_scene and run_window (usage quiet_needs_frames, frames, exercise_needs_quiet and script_frame_only at window.rs:288-299; GuiFrame::open and content refusals at :303/:308 before EventLoop at :312; event_loop, create_window, handle, timeout, focus violation, never_started-type window states via App::finish; Vulkan refusals; success) ends in one finish (diag.rs:105), and a panic ends in one send (diag.rs:109). studio-vk: parse and caller refusals send one frame (studio-vk.rs:56-61); help sends none (returns at :14-17); the run() Help arm (:53) is unreachable (main returns on Ok(Help) first) and its comment 'still sends its frame' contradicts the docs, a nit. Zero-frame paths: F1 (argv or parse panic before HostRun), F3 (a reused HostRun), the unreachable HostRun::new error at :28-33 (Budget::new(0, 0) is constant), panic=abort and double panic (named by the builder). Two-frame paths: none found. send() refuses a second frame, and no caller of finish exists after an entry.
answers.catch_unwind_soundness: Sound. The closure captures only &args, never the HostRun, so host state is intact when the panic is caught. AssertUnwindSafe hides nothing observable, because the panic is always resumed. winit 0.30.13 on Windows catches callback panics in runner.catch_unwind and resumes them after reset_runner (event_loop.rs:422-425, runner.rs:170-192). Vulkan's debug messenger (hsk-studio-vulkan owner.rs:193, extern "system") is written not to panic and recovers poisoned locks; a panic there would abort, with no frame, the same class as panic=abort. Leaks: F5 (the foreground watcher thread). Not checked: whether Live's Drop is safe after the winit Window field drops first on an unwind (App field order: window before live; the normal path releases explicitly in App::release).
answers.delivery_failure_and_exit_code: Library entries: never. observed returns the run's result, and a_refused_delivery_never_changes_the_run_result pins it. studio-vk: an --observe file that does not open is Unavailable, the exit code is unchanged, and the note goes to stderr. Exception F2: a broken stderr turns the note's eprintln! into a panic (exit 101, no receipt).
answers.jsonl_line_and_atomicity: Well formed: schema and class are constants, frame_hex is lowercase hex, and the numbers are u64 or null. No caller text reaches the line; ids are only inside the hex frame. Offsets match the observe wire v1 header (HSKO, version, outcome byte 5, failure byte 6, progress flag, then BE u64 correlation 8..16, revision 16..24, sequence 24..32). The line is built in full, then sent with one write_all on a per-send File opened with append(true), so on local NTFS a line of at most about 4.2 KB (frame limit 2048 bytes as hex plus fields) goes in one WriteFile at EOF and does not interleave with other appenders. Limits: a crash in the middle of a write can leave a line without a newline, so the next append joins it; append atomicity is not guaranteed on network shares; the stderr fallback mixes the line with usage, error and panic text (the tests filter by schema).
answers.caller_flag_spoofing: The flags are self-declared, a stated limit as for the harness CLI; nothing proves a grant. Injection: none. Values pass accord bounds (ActorContext: 1..=128 bytes, no control character; DomainId::parse) and appear only hex-encoded. caller_default comes from the parse result, not from input. On every command line that parse accepts, run_flags tokenises exactly as parse does: VALUE_FLAGS lists all 15 value flags of parse plus the 4 new ones, and the mode-only flags (--out, --capture, --frames, --deadline-s) appear only where parse accepts them. A divergence such as offscreen --frames --actor exists only on lines parse refuses, and parse's refusal takes precedence (command.and_then at studio-vk.rs:35). A refused caller is attributed to the asset-local context with caller_default true, so the line says so. The default actor is a literal in new code (cli.rs Caller::asset_local). That is a lead-ruled deviation from HOST INTEGRATION (4) (point 5), marked by caller_default and pinned equal to harness-view's Viewer context under [document] (round unit hsk-studio-native-host = [["document"]], .config/round-features.toml:51).
answers.tests_pinning_implementation: None only pins the implementation. The frame tests check count, class, outcome, correlation, sequence and the caller's ids inside the frame bytes, and the studio-vk tests decode the line. The panic proof is the unit test diag.rs a_panicking_run_sends_one_failure_frame_and_keeps_unwinding on observed itself. That entries reach observed is shown by reading (offscreen.rs:45-47, window.rs:284-286), not by a panicking entry. Gaps: no binary-level success line (needs the GPU), no binary exit-code test under a failing sink (F2), no reused HostRun (F3), no non-Unicode argv (F1). The 18 call sites assert exactly [Terminal] and keep every existing assertion. The four observed()/Frames helpers are copies; a shared tests/support module would remove three, a style point only.
answers.focus_and_foreground: No new test opens a winit window or takes focus. The window::run calls in the new test refuse at window.rs:288 or at :303/:308, before EventLoop at :312. The studio-vk children are refused in parse or caller before any device. The only device run is the offscreen clear scene, with no window, and the whole package is in the render-gpu nextest group (.config/nextest.toml:31). Child console windows: F4.
answers.correlation: studio-vk mints correlation 1 for every process (TransientCorrelation::new().next()). That matches the harness CLI (harness/src/cli.rs:1146), but runs appended to one --observe file cannot be told apart by correlation and sequence. See lead_questions.

lead_questions: F3: refuse a finished HostRun in observed (typed, opens nothing) in this lane, or accept &mut HostRun reuse as a caller error and say so in the HostRun doc?

Correlation: the lane block says the host run's correlation comes from the caller, but studio-vk always mints 1 and has no --correlation. Add an optional --correlation (u64), or record the binary's correlation as host-minted?

--observe that cannot be opened: the approved design reads '--observe PATH writes a JSONL sink, falling back to stderr'. As built, stderr is used only when --observe is absent; an unopenable --observe loses the frame and leaves only 'observe_undelivered unavailable' on stderr. Is that the intended reading, or should LineSink write the line to stderr when the file does not open?
F5: name the Watch thread leak in this lane's v4_06 and leave the fix to a window lane, or extend the owned paths to window.rs Watch?
